issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (raised ways x part-0 ways laid after them; the catalogue pairs raised with edit and epoch only by keyword). Once a raised way stands, a part-0 way laid across its under-deck strip has no rule keeping it off the piers or out of a `vault` span. §2.7's support step (3) slides piers off 'a part-0 way's corridor' (base l.2528-2529) and the span rule opens a span over a way (l.2575-2577) only for the ways standing when they run, and nothing re-runs them for a later way: only (6) for a trace or moat and §4.11's carve for a channel (l.8128). The later ways carry no support obstacle: §4.3's lattice costs (l.5559-5563: water, reservation, wall, existing fabric, land value, the class grade limit) name none; S5c's legality (l.5855-5860: spines, shores, wall setback bands, reservations, the stage boundary, walls, water) none; §7.1's ground `drawWay` (l.10295-10297) and E-07 have no bend or refusal for a pier (V09's `bend.raised.*` keys cover raised strokes only). V06 runs `raisedWays` (step 10a) before `growth` (step 14; V06 l.1004, l.1008), and the growth's S5-S13 on new faces re-runs no support step. Only a raised course (V06 §3.19 (5), l.2797), a new trace (V06 §3.7.6 (5), l.1581-1582), stage 2's own laying (V01 §3.17.3 (3), l.2469-2477: 'never along the strip, never through a pier') and S8's holes (§4.6 l.6375-6379) keep off the piers. So an epoch growing a stage over a standing aqueduct's or viaduct's land (H-AQUA's case), an epoch route re-solve, or a hand road drawn across a viaduct lays a street over pier rings or through an arch-vault chamber. Masonry piers stand every 8-15 m, each 0.2 of its span wide (V11 l.3949), so most such crossings meet one. Nothing catches it: §5.3 holds no support invariant, T110-2's 'zero junctions' passes, and S8's holes keep only plots out. A street through a masonry pier is an impossible result on a CITY epoch's common path, the same class as 'a support standing in water'.
issues.required_change: Pipeline: §4.3 *Lattice and costs* adds: 'A standing raised way's support rings and the under-deck strips of its `vault` spans are impassable to every route and growth proposal on ground part 0. Its under-deck strip is crossed only under an `open` span whose clear width holds the way's corridor + `raisedWays.structure.clearWidthM` and whose soffit meets §2.7's clearance for the crossed class, within ± `raisedWays.structure.squareDeg` of square to the deck. The route's crossing shifts along the strip to the nearest such span, else the route takes another course by F-ROUTE's ladder.' §4.4 S5c's legality adds: 'a proposal meeting a standing raised way's strip anywhere else is deflected along it to the nearest such span, or ends at the strip as at a reservation.' This is the one rule V01 §3.17.3 (3) states for stage 2. Its two cells move to V11 §3.24.2's `raisedWays.structure` (`clearWidthM` 1 m, `squareDeg` 30°), and V01 §3.17.3 (3) cites §4.3 (principle (9): one mechanism; equivalence: V01's crossing rule, ladder and values unchanged). Ends (R3-01): determinism §7.1, a ground `drawWay` or a moved way crossing a standing raised way's strip elsewhere is bent at its dry run to the nearest such span (E-07's row; V09 §4.9 `bend.raised.underSpan`); V06 §3.6 and §3.19 cite §4.3 for the growth and route re-solves; scope §13.2 T110-2 adds 'an H-AQUA epoch growing a stage over a standing aqueduct's land, an epoch route re-solved under a viaduct, and a hand road drawn across one: 0 way corridors over a support ring or a `vault` span, every crossing under an `open` span'. At generation, VEW-r3-02's re-run slides the piers off the ways S5b and S5c grew.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (the support step x S7 at generation). At generation the support step reads obstacles that later stages lay. It runs 'after its course and deck level are fixed' (§2.7 l.2523-2524), and the raised parts commit at S4 (viaducts), S5b (a stage's viaducts) and S6's end (elevated roads and aqueducts) (§4.3 *The slot* l.5634-5636; §4.1's stage table). S7 comes after S6. It cuts the wall strips (`Enceinte.strips`, 'the two L1 wall-strip faces S7 cuts off', l.2255) and writes the band's thickness (`thicknessCm` 'written by S7', l.2258; a `parapet` run's by S7's `stretchClass`). It also claims the gate plazas and lays the quays, piers and moles (l.7515-7527, l.7557, l.7635-7640). S5c grows the secondaries round an S4 or S5b viaduct before then. So (3)'s obstacles do not yet exist when the step runs: 'an enceinte's wall strip (`Enceinte.strips`)', 'the strip's setback and glacis parts, the berm' (l.2530-2531, l.2545-2546), 'a part-0 way's corridor (… a pier's, a mole's or a quay's deck among them)', and 'a square … or a reservation'. No text runs the step again after S7. (6), new this round, re-runs it 'in the same commit' as an S5a trace (l.2559-2563) and slides 'the stations in the new strips' setbacks, glacis, berm or channel', but S7 has not cut those strips; only the channel S5a carves exists. Two builders differ. One leaves the piers where the commit put them: in the setback and glacis, in a gate plaza, under a quay, against T110-2's '0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat' (l.18225-18231), with no §5.3 invariant to catch it. Another derives the strips early from values S7 has not written.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step adds: 'At generation the support step runs once more on every raised way after S7's batches and before S7b (1), its span rule then running at its eager time, each station keeping its key by (5). The obstacles then standing include S5b's and S5c's ways and S7's wall strips, gate plazas, castle paths, quays, piers and moles. The run at a raised part's commit (S4, S5b, S6) and (6)'s run at an S5a trace read the obstacles standing then, the channel S5a carves among them; the strips are taken at this later run.' Pipeline end (R3-01): §4.3 *The slot* and §4.8's lead state 'after S7, §2.7's support step re-runs on every raised way, its keys kept (§2.7 (5))'. T110-2's CITY masonry aqueduct and its c14 viaduct fixtures already run at generation and then bar it.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (a trace meeting a raised way's ramp or foot; opened by this round's (6)). (6) defines a trace that crosses a standing raised way between its feet at deck level. Nothing defines a trace, its strips or its moat that meet the raised way's ramp or a foot. The feet are ground vertices where the ramps or stairs meet part 0 (§2.7 `RaisedWayRecord.feet`, l.2287; §4.6 l.6617-6618, ramps at the class grade). Nothing ties the trace's place to them. At generation a later stage's boundary on the S3 lattice may fall at a valley's rim, where an S4 viaduct comes down. At an epoch V06 §3.7.1's widening counts supports as footprints but no foot or ramp (V06 l.1448-1450), and V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s cost field makes only the supports impassable (l.1581-1582). Three outcomes follow. (6)'s crossing station is then 'one added' on the ramp: a raised gate whose tower carries a deck a metre above the ground. The strip's setback and glacis, or the berm and the channel S5a carves 'outside the outer half-band and a berm' (l.5805-5806), take the ramp and the foot. S5a's *Outer moats* adds 'no part-0 deck' for a raised gate because 'the deck itself' crosses the channel (l.5809-5812). So a part-0 arterial leaving a foot between the band and the channel's outer bank meets the channel with no deck, against §5.3's hard invariant 'a way crosses water only on a deck' (l.9114), or the foot's ground vertex lies in the water face itself. (6)'s give-way names only a clear span past `maxClearSpanM` or a pier past `maxPierM`.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) adds: 'A crossing station stands where the deck is at its level, never on a ramp or a stair. Where the new trace, its strips or its moat channel would meet a ramp, a stair or a foot of the raised way (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`), the trace gives way as for a span past its bound. S5a: its stage trace takes the next lattice boundary node off the ramp, reported. V06: it retraces by the margin rule and waits (`walls.waited`). A hand `drawWall`: its dry run bends the trace clear of it (item 101 R2). So no foot, ramp or stair stands in a setback, glacis, berm or channel, and the part-0 way beyond a foot never meets the channel.' Ends (R3-01): §4.4 S5a *Outer moats* (pipeline) cites it beside 'no part-0 deck added for it'. V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s continuity bullet adds the ramp and the foot to what makes a trace retrace and wait. §13.2 T110-2 (scope) adds 'a stage-2 moated ring whose lattice boundary falls on an S4 viaduct's ramp at a valley rim: the trace moved off the ramp, reported, the foot and ramp outside the strips and the channel, the raised way kept'.

issues.claim: A crossing station's support is the wall. (3) makes 'that station's support `ring` … the band's stretch under the deck, the wall's own masonry (no pier raised, no pier-height test)' (l.2543-2545), and round 3 holds that stretch while the deck stands (l.2546-2553). The raised way's own support ops still treat that `supports` entry as a pier, with no rule tying them to the stretch's `condition`. (a) V06 §3.19.2 (3)'s salvage takes 'a support both of whose spans are ruined or cleared … → `dismantle` on the support (cleared)' (V06 l.2900-2901). At a station that is the wall's masonry under the deck. §2.7 (3) instead makes the stretch 'an ordinary run' from the first epoch after both spans have fallen, decaying by V06 §3.7.7. So the same masonry has two outcomes: taken as the raised way's salvage, or kept as a wall run. (b) V06 §3.19.2 (4)'s `topple` 'takes a support, weighted by its height, and breaks both spans beside it' (l.2908). A station has no pier height, and a toppled station leaves its support `ruined` while the held stretch's `condition` stays `standing`. (c) A landfall breaches the stretch and ruins the support (V05 §3.16's wall and pier rows, V05 l.1338 and l.1342; §2.7 (3)). V06 §3.19.2 (5)'s `repairRaised` then re-stands the spans beside it, 'its ruined supports with it' (l.2917). No text repairs the stretch, so the repaired deck stands on a `breached` gate tower, or on a stretch that the ordinary run's decay (V06 §3.7.7 (2)) dismantled meanwhile. Two units state two outcomes for one case: MAJOR by R3-03 (b).
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3) adds: 'A crossing station's `supports` entry carries no `state` of its own. It reads its stretch's `condition`: `standing`, `worn` or `patched` is a standing support; `breached` or `dismantled` is a ruined one. The raised way's support ops pass over it: V06 §3.19.2 (3)'s salvage `dismantle` and (4)'s `topple` never take it, and its stretch decays as the wall's once both spans have fallen. A landfall's breach of the stretch ruins the spans beside it (V05 §3.16). A `repairRaised` of a span beside a station whose stretch is `breached` or `dismantled`, whether V06 §3.19.2 (5)'s or a hand Repair, first repairs that stretch by `repairWall` in the same batch, in item 114's patch material, so no deck stands on a fallen wall.' Ends (R3-01): V06 §3.19.2 (3)-(5) cite it, the salvage and topple candidates excluding a station and the repair naming its wall step. V05 §3.16's raised-way pier row adds '(a crossing station's support is its wall stretch, §2.7: the wall row's breach)'. §13.2's item-114 group (scope) adds 'a landfall over a raised gate, then the deck's repair: the stretch repaired with the deck, never a deck on a breached run; a station whose spans have both fallen keeps its stretch as a wall run, never dismantled as a support'.

issues.claim: The enumerations of what (6) covers are narrower than its rule. (6)'s 'a later stage's S5a trace and outer moat at generation' (l.2560-2561) and §4.8's '(a later stage's trace across an S4 viaduct, elevated road or aqueduct …)' (l.7562-7563) both miss one case. Stage k's S5b may raise a viaduct (l.5824). That viaduct is committed before stage k's own S5a trace (§4.1's S5 row: S5b's L1 batch, then S5a's), and the trace can cross it, but stage k's trace is not 'a later stage's'. And at generation an elevated road or an aqueduct is laid at S6's end, after every trace (l.5634-5636), so no generation trace crosses one standing. (6)'s governing clause ('a trace or moat laid across a standing raised way') covers the case, so a builder reaches it. Only the lists and T110-2's fixtures name less.
issues.required_change: §2.7 (6): 'a stage's S5a trace and outer moat at generation across an S4 viaduct or a viaduct an S5b laid before it, the stage's own included'. Pipeline end, §4.8: '(at generation a stage's trace across an S4 or S5b viaduct; at an epoch, or by a hand `drawWall`, any trace across a standing raised way, its crossing station put on the trace by §2.7's support step (6))'. Scope's T110-2 adds 'a stage-2 S5b viaduct crossed by stage 2's own moated ring'.
